assumptions.condition: The mixed graph \(G\) has no loops or repeated edges of either type.
For every distinct \(u,v\in V\), \((u,v)\in D\) or \((v,u)\in D\) implies \(\{u,v\}\notin B\).

novel.justification: The condition describes sparse bow-free causal systems whose inclusion-minimal nonidentifiability witnesses involve at most three manipulable variables; it includes all private-guard realizations, bidirected trees of radius two, and the first nonempty bow-free singleton obstruction class.

definitions.name: Singleton-target hedge family
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)=\{F\subseteq V:\{s\}\subsetneq F,\ B[F]\text{ is connected, and every }v\in F\text{ has a directed path to }s\text{ in }D[F]\}\).

definitions.name: Minimum-cost identifying intervention
definitions.construction: Choose \(A^\star\in\arg\min_{A\subseteq V^{-}}\sum_{v\in A}c(v)\) subject to \(A\cap R\neq\varnothing\) for every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\); its value is \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\).

definitions.name: Natural residual-hedge covering relaxation
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)=\min_{y\in[0,1]^{V^{-}}}\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v\) subject to \(\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\) for all \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).

definitions.name: Ordered private-guard expansion
definitions.construction: For each \(u\in U\), create \(x_u\) and add \(s\leftrightarrow x_u\). For each \(e=\{u,v\}\in E\) with \(u\prec v\), create a private \(z_e\) and add exactly \(x_u\to x_v\), \(x_v\to z_e\), \(z_e\to s\), and \(z_e\leftrightarrow x_u\). The resulting graph is \(G_H\).

definitions.name: Parent-spouse threshold rounding
definitions.construction: Given an optimal fractional solution \(y\), scan the finitely many breakpoints of \(A_t=\{p\in P_s:y_p\geq t\}\cup\{b\in T_s:y_b\geq1/2-t\}\) over \(0<t<1/2\), and return the cheapest \(A_t\).

definitions.name: Promised-rank obstruction enumerator
definitions.construction: Test every \(R\subseteq V^{-}\) with \(|R|\leq3\) by bidirected connectivity and directed reachability in \(G[R\cup\{s\}]\), retain it exactly when it is a hedge residual and no proper subset is one, and order outputs lexicographically.

definitions.name: Fixed-point rank-recognition handle
definitions.construction: Analyze the decision problem \(r(G,s)\leq3\) by combining alternating restriction to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\) with deletion-based extraction of an inclusion-minimal hedge certificate.

statements.statement: Every \(F\in\mathsf{Hdg}(G,s)\) has \(|F|\geq4\). A four-vertex \(F\) is a hedge if and only if the unordered pairs of \(D[F]\) form a spanning path oriented toward \(s\) and \(B[F]\) is the complementary spanning path. Consequently, \(r(G,s)\leq2\) implies \(\mathcal C(G,s)=\varnothing\). If \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) and \(|R|=3\), then \(R\subseteq P_s\cup T_s\), \(R\cap P_s\neq\varnothing\), \(R\cap T_s\neq\varnothing\), and \(P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing\).
statements.justification: This edge-count characterization locates the first nonzero obstruction rank and creates the two-sided incidence structure used by the approximation theorem.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash establish polynomial optimization when minimal hedge size is at most two in a more general model, but do not classify bow-free singleton hedges or show that ranks one and two are empty in this model.
statements.consumer: A rank-aware preprocessing layer can return the empty intervention without invoking RC2, Gurobi, or hedge enumeration whenever the promised rank is at most two.

statements.statement: For every ordered finite simple graph \(H=(U,E)\), the graph \(G_H\) is bow-free and acyclic, its bidirected subgraph is a tree of radius at most two centered at \(s\), and \(\mathcal C(G_H,s)=\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E\}\). Hence \(r(G_H,s)=3\) when \(E\neq\varnothing\), and \(r(G_H,s)=0\) otherwise.
statements.justification: Exact reverse inclusion, rather than mere construction of intended hedges, is the load-bearing causal-clutter representation result.
statements.gap: The two-auxiliary reduction of Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash does not realize exactly one three-element minimal residual per source edge and does not preserve a radius-two bidirected tree.
statements.consumer: The theorem turns graph benchmarks into certified rank-three MCID instances for the min-cost-intervention implementation and for solver regression tests.

statements.statement: Assign unit cost to every vertex of \(G_H\). Every vertex cover \(C\subseteq U\) maps to the intervention \(\{x_u:u\in C\}\) with the same cost, and every feasible intervention maps in polynomial time, by replacing each selected \(z_e\) with an endpoint of \(e\), to a vertex cover of no larger cost. Therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\). The reduction is an \(L\)-reduction with constants one, so rank-three MCID is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard even with unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree; the \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness remains for source graphs of maximum degree three.
statements.justification: Objective preservation identifies the exact complexity transition at the first nonempty rank rather than importing generic three-hitting-set hardness.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove unrestricted MCID hardness, while Alimonti and Kann supply cubic vertex-cover hardness; neither gives a promise-preserving rank-three causal realization.
statements.consumer: The result supplies structured hard instances on which the RC2 and Gurobi formulations can be evaluated without uncontrolled hedge rank.

statements.statement: Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time after promised-rank enumeration.
statements.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
statements.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
statements.consumer: The theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.

statements.statement: The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\) over unit-cost bow-free singleton instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and radius-two bidirected trees equals two. For \(G_{K_n}\), the ratio is \(2-2/n\). Under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on this same promised-rank class.
statements.justification: A matching gap family and conditional lower bound certify that factor two is the exact polynomial frontier under the standard conjecture.
statements.gap: Khot and Regev establish the threshold for vertex cover, and Singh characterizes the source LP gap; no published result transfers the threshold to a bounded-rank causal-effect-identification design class.
statements.consumer: Algorithm designers can treat a certified factor-two rank-three solution as worst-case optimal under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), focusing engineering effort on instance-specific improvement.

statements.statement: For every fixed promised rank bound \(r_0\), all inclusion-minimal residual hedges can be output exactly once in time \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\) and polynomial space by subset testing and canonical ordering. At \(r_0=3\) in the present bow-free singleton model, the runtime is \(O(|V|^3\operatorname{poly}(|V|))\). Given \(k\), branching on an uncovered residual returns the least-cost feasible intervention among sets of cardinality at most \(k\), or certifies none exists, in \(O(3^k\operatorname{poly}(|V|,L))\), where \(L\) is the cost-encoding length.
statements.justification: The proposition supplies the explicit obstruction list assumed by the LP and scopes exact weighted search to a supplied cardinality bound.
statements.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash note polynomial subset enumeration at fixed hedge size, while Fernau assumes an explicit hyperedge list; neither supplies exact-once causal output together with the bounded-cardinality scope correction.
statements.consumer: The enumerator is a rank-informed front end for Akbari and coauthors' software and for Elahi and coauthors' exact solver encodings.

statements.statement: Enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three, optimize or two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails, deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
statements.justification: The interface safely exploits low rank without pretending to recognize the promise from a successful run.
statements.gap: The WPMAX-SAT and ILP formulations of Elahi and coauthors solve unrestricted MCID but do not return a violated-rank certificate, while explicit bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume the promise externally.
statements.consumer: RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified solution guarantee or a concrete large hedge to pass to the unrestricted backend.

statements.statement: Determine whether deciding \(r(G,s)\leq3\) for finite simple bow-free ADMGs with singleton target \(s\) has a polynomial-time algorithm, or whether it is \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-complete, using the fixed-point hedge oracle to certify \(r(G,s)>3\).
statements.justification: Promise recognition is the genuine unresolved algorithmic boundary left visible by the certifying interface.
statements.gap: Neither bounded-size enumeration in Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash nor the solver encodings of Elahi and coauthors classify the complexity of recognizing that no larger minimal hedge exists.
statements.consumer: A resolution determines whether low-rank preprocessing can be invoked automatically or must remain a promise-or-counterexample workflow.

sampling_model.design: Deterministic selection of proxy-intervention distributions indexed by \(A\); the design randomness and finite-sample allocation are outside this combinatorial identification scope.
sampling_model.units: Vertices of a fixed finite semi-Markovian causal graph \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: Acquisition of the interventional laws associated with the selected proxy variables in \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity required by the imported generalized-identification semantics is held fixed and is not strengthened by the optimization results.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the target is experiment acquisition sufficient for graphical identification, not estimation from finite samples.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix D.2 gives polynomial optimization when every minimal hedge residual has size at most two, while fixed larger size only makes enumeration polynomial and leaves hitting set exponential.
Theorems 1--2 encode MCID feasibility as SAT and then WPMAX-SAT or ILP, and the conclusion leaves efficient approximation as future work.
Theorem 6 and Corollaries 2--3 make hedges complete graphical witnesses for failure of interventional identification.
Optimal fractional vertex-packing solutions have half-integral basic optima and their integral coordinates persist in an integral optimum.
Theorem 3.1 establishes APX-completeness of minimum vertex cover on cubic graphs.
Assuming the Unique Games Conjecture, minimum vertex cover has no polynomial approximation factor below two.
The vertex-cover LP integrality gap on a graph is \(2-2/\chi^f(G)\).
Weighted \(d\)-Hitting Set with an explicit hyperedge list admits parameterized search-tree algorithms.

tldr: Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for bow-free singleton-target ADMGs. Four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes the edge clutter of every ordered simple graph exactly, yielding unit-cost NP and APX hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. The same path classification partitions every rank-three residual across target parents and spouses, which gives a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm; complete-graph expansions attain gap \(2-2/n\), and the Khot--Regev threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\). Promised enumeration and an optimizer-or-rank-violation interface connect the theorem to existing exact solvers, while unrestricted rank-three recognition remains an explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: The published MCID frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness. It does not identify the first nonempty bow-free singleton rank or its causal-specific approximation ratio.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition, yet the class is expressive enough to realize every graph edge clutter through private guards.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact four-vertex obstruction classification and representation theorem, transfers objective-preserving hardness, derives a tight factor-two LP frontier, and gives a certifying interface that is useful without asserting an unrestricted rank recognizer.

related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the complete hedge obstruction used to interpret residual hitting as causal identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash formulate MCID as minimum-weight hedge hitting, prove unrestricted hardness, and settle bounded residual size through two; their Appendix D.2 is the direct boundary this paper continues. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow the immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the rounding argument, although the proposed parent-spouse threshold proof is stated directly on causal residuals. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover APX hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred by the exact private-guard realization. Singh's LP-gap formula motivates the complete-graph family but is not claimed to be sharpened. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine.
technical_internal_limitation: The private-guard reverse inclusion and the parent-spouse rounding are universal informal arguments that require independent proof checking. The solver interface does not recognize \(r(G,s)\leq3\) from a successful run. Weighted \(O(3^k)\) exact search is claimed only with a supplied cardinality bound, not as an unconstrained optimizer parameterized by an unknown optimum cardinality.
honest_scope: The central classification, exact realization, hardness transfer, rounding bound, and gap family are theorem targets. General positivity-based equivalence between hedge hitting and interventional identification, source complexity theorems, and rational LP solution are imported. The complexity of recognizing rank at most three, planar bounded-degree causal realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open. The reduction to a one-edge source graph recovers the unique four-vertex hedge, while \(r(G,s)\leq2\) reduces to the empty-intervention result, providing the required standard sanity checks.

threads.settled: MCID is minimum-weight hitting of minimal hedges; unrestricted instances are hard, and residual size at most two is polynomial.

threads.settled: The graph vertex-cover relaxation has half-integral structure and supports threshold-two approximation machinery.
threads.adapted_technique: Use threshold charging, but derive feasibility from the causal parent-spouse partition instead of assuming a graph-edge LP.

threads.settled: Under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), graph vertex cover cannot be approximated within \(2-\epsilon\).
threads.adapted_technique: Compose the gap with an objective-preserving causal realization and explicitly remove guard selections without cost increase.

novelty_justification: The two closest results are Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash's bounded-hedge theorem and Elahi and coauthors' solver formulation. The strict delta from the former is an exact bow-free singleton classification showing that residual ranks one and two are empty, followed by exact realization of every graph edge clutter at rank three with one private guard and a radius-two bidirected tree. The strict delta from the latter is a proved polynomial weighted factor-two approximation, a matching causal LP-gap family, and a conditional lower bound, rather than a faster exact encoding or heuristic. The theorem does not advertise generic hitting-set enumeration or LP solving as novel. Bounded searches through September 2026 found no closer paper that states the same rank-three representability or approximation frontier.
message: Authored and validated the cold-start typed proposal core with nine ranked seeds, three deepened candidates, an exact rank-three kernel, and the required literature handoff fields.
